mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) predicts weakening consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND UNRATE > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of more than 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises >0.3pp for 3 months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing output, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by >0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month by >1% AND HOUST > previous month by >1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such co-rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% for two consecutive months, real interest rates rise, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL < 200 (i.e., <2%) for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative under this regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4% in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >0.4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such PAYEMS surges (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a monthly increase in RSAFS of more than 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns within the following week.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises by >0.5% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.10).
